ex.3: Signal from 360° on heading 315° arrives at relative bearing 045°, a quadrantal (inter-cardinal) bearing: maximum error. 225° and 135° arrive at 270° and 180° relative: no error.
ex.10: With RB 000 the nose follows the beacon; the heading falls (turning left) because the wind is pushing you right: right (starboard) drift.
ex.15: Outbound with RB 184 means 4° starboard drift. Coming back on the reciprocal, the same wind gives 4° port drift, so the nose points 4° right of the station: RB 356.
ex.30: Range ∝ √power: double the range needs four times the power.
